# Rung S of climb batch 33: the library selector

problem: the compiled path reads only the compiler's prelude, so a wall that only the one library shows has no test under the gate; probe Y's selector met them in scratch only: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/PROBES.md:69-82`
spec: none: `grep -rln 'FORTRESS_LIBRARY\|fortress\.library\|caches-one' Specification Documentation` prints nothing, and no sentence names a selector or a caches folder: none
precedent: probe Y's hunks of `Shell.useCompilerLibraries()`, `WellKnownNames.compiledPathUsesOneLibrary` and `bin/fortress_classpath` (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/probe-y.patch:561-582`, `:670-688`, `:1160-1182`); the stamp's form for `cache0` and `cache1` and the testFast track's form (`fastTrack`, `testLibrary`, `LibraryJUTest`): `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/LibraryJUTest.java:28-42`
deviation: the selection is read once in `ProjectProperties`, and `WellKnownNames` takes it from there, not read in `WellKnownNames` as probe Y and the brief place it: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/repository/ProjectProperties.java:290`
deviation: `useCompilerLibraries()` sets no `ByteCodeWriter.keepFirstCopyOfAClass`, probe Y's hack 7, which this rung does not own: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:377`
deviation: the selection's caches folder is `${REPOSITORY}/caches-one` unless a property or the environment names one, whatever the configuration's `fortress.caches` line says; probe Y named it by hand: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/repository/ProjectProperties.java:299`
deviation: every testFast track pins `FORTRESS_LIBRARY`, empty for the prelude's four, as it pins `FORTRESS_THREADS`: `build.xml:1223`
deviation: `.gitignore` ignores the new folder, a file the brief does not name: `.gitignore:29`
historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/WellKnownNames.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/repository/ProjectProperties.java`, `bin/fortress_classpath`, `bin/run_classpath` and `build.xml`, each in `a874948ac`: `build.xml:47`

One launch worked this rung. Commit `21e155ea9e` holds the code and the tests; every run below that is not marked "base" ran on it. The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0).

## What changed and why

**The selector** (fork S1). `ProjectProperties.compiledPathUsesOneLibrary` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/repository/ProjectProperties.java:283-291`) is true where the property `fortress.library`, or else the environment variable `FORTRESS_LIBRARY`, is `one`, read once when the class loads, as probe Y read it (`probe-y.patch:683-684`). Any other value, or none, is the prelude. `WellKnownNames.compiledPathUsesOneLibrary` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/WellKnownNames.java:143-150`) gives it to the compiler. `Shell.useCompilerLibraries()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:373-388`) points `WellKnownNames` and `Types` at `FortressLibrary`, `FortressBuiltin` and `AnyType` where it is set, and at the prelude's names where not; the desugaring switches stay the compile command's. Nothing of the code generator follows it (`NamingCzar`, `CodeGen`, `runtimeValues/` unchanged).

The commands that follow it are those that call `useCompilerLibraries()` (`Shell.java:414-502`): `compile`, `link`, `build`, `api`, `compare`, `parse`, `unparse`, `disambiguate`, `desugar`, `grammar`, `typecheck`, `test-coercion`, `help` and the usage message, and `junit`, whose compiles and links go through `subMain`. `fortress run` follows it through the class path script's caches folder only (below). Walk, `test` and `typecheck-old` keep reading the interpreter's library; under the selection they keep their caches in the selection's folder too, since `ProjectProperties.CACHES` is one value for the JVM:

    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one bin/fortress tests/BooleanOps.fss          (from ProjectFortress/)
    rc=0
    ls ../default_repository/caches-one/interpreter_cache | grep -c BooleanOps
    1

**The caches folder** (fork S2). `ProjectProperties.CACHES` (`ProjectProperties.java:293-302`) is the folder that the property `fortress.caches` or `FORTRESS_CACHES` names; else, under the selection, `${REPOSITORY}/caches-one`; else, as before, the configuration's `${FORTRESS_REPOSITORY}/caches`. `bin/fortress_classpath:25-31` and `bin/run_classpath:25-31` take the same default from `FORTRESS_LIBRARY`. `build.xml` gives the folder the stamp of `cache0` and `cache1`: the property `cacheOne` (`build.xml:44-47`), `cleanCache` (`:367`, `:376`), `checkCaches` (`:531-534`, `:553-558`, `:565`) and the end of `compileAll` (`:863`). `.gitignore:28-29` ignores the folder; without it every build would leave an untracked folder, and a base build whose `git status --porcelain` prints a line cannot seed a worktree (`.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/worktrees.md`, "Finding or building a base build").

    bin/fortress expand CACHES                                   /home/user/fortress-library-selector/default_repository/caches
    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one bin/fortress expand CACHES              /home/user/fortress-library-selector/default_repository/caches-one
    JAVA_FLAGS="... -Dfortress.library=one" bin/fortress expand CACHES   .../default_repository/caches-one
    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one FORTRESS_CACHES=/tmp/x bin/fortress expand CACHES   /tmp/x
    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=One bin/fortress expand CACHES              .../default_repository/caches

The stamp, on the edit's first build, an unchanged build, and `ant cleanCache`:

    ant compileAll          [echo] Caches .../default_repository/caches started again, empty
                            [echo] Caches .../default_repository/caches-one started again, empty
    ant compileAll          [echo] Caches .../default_repository/caches kept
    (unchanged)             [echo] Caches .../default_repository/caches-one kept
    ant cleanCache          [delete] Deleting directory .../default_repository/caches-one
                            [echo] Caches .../default_repository/caches-one started again, empty

After `cleanCache`, `default_repository/caches-one/implementation.stamp` equals `ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp` (`diff` printed nothing).

**The track** (fork S4). `ProjectFortress/one_library_tests/` holds the track's `.test` files. `OneLibraryJUTest` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/OneLibraryJUTest.java`) runs them as `LibraryJUTest` runs `library_tests`; without the selection it is one failing test that names it:

    java ... junit.textui.TestRunner com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.OneLibraryJUTest      (no FORTRESS_LIBRARY)
    1) oneLibrarySelected(...OneLibraryJUTest$1)junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: one_library_tests runs only where FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one selects the one library, as ant testOneLibrary does
    Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0

`fastTrack` takes a `library` attribute, empty by default, and sets `FORTRESS_LIBRARY` to it (`build.xml:1201-1207`, `:1223`); `ant testOneLibrary` (`build.xml:1146-1156`) runs the track alone with `library="one"` and private caches `ProjectFortress/test-caches/fast-onelibrary`, and `testFast` runs it as a fifth track in its parallel of four threads, so it starts when one of the four ends (`build.xml:1275-1280`); the misc track leaves the class out (`build.xml:1262`). The compile steps run in the JUnit JVM, which reads the variable; the run step is a `bin/fortress run` process that inherits it with `FORTRESS_CACHES` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:542-566`). The gate's summary takes the track as a new row, `fast-onelibrary/OneLibraryJUTest`, since `gate_summary` reads every `fast-*` folder (`explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh:33`), and `gate_compare` prints nothing for a suite the last summary lacks (`gate-functions.sh:46-58`).

The track's first tests:

- `OneLibraryHalf.fss` and `.test`: probe Y's `Half.fss`, `q: QQ = 1/2` and `println(q)`, with `println("REACHED")` first; it compiles.
- `OneLibraryPrintBig.fss` and `.test`: `run(): () = println(big(7))`. `big` is declared by the one library on each integer type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:569`) and by no prelude file (row 349); it compiles.
- `XXXOneLibraryRunHalf.test`: `tests=OneLibraryHalf`, `run`, `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED`. The run dies at the first library class before `run()` prints: the one library has no jars (new row NEW-S-1; rows 874, 624 and 315).

## The tests: the failing run on the base, the passing run

The failing run, through the harness, on the base's code under the selection, 17:49:07Z to 17:49:09Z; the edit was first built at 17:52:04Z (`tmp/rung-library-selector/build1.txt` born then):

    cd ProjectFortress && FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base37 \
        tmp/rung-library-selector/old-caches junit one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf.test \
        one_library_tests/OneLibraryPrintBig.test one_library_tests/XXXOneLibraryRunHalf.test
    . compile .../one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf .../OneLibraryHalf.fss:7:6:
        QQ is undefined.
    F. compile .../one_library_tests/OneLibraryPrintBig .../OneLibraryPrintBig.fss:5:21-22:
        Variable big is not defined.
    Tests run: 3,  Failures: 2,  Errors: 0

The passing run, the last after the last change of code (`21e155ea9e`), the onelibrary track of `ant testFast` (`ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/fast-onelibrary/TEST-com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.OneLibraryJUTest.txt`):

    ant testFast
     compile .../one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf  OK (time = 57854ms)
     compile .../one_library_tests/OneLibraryPrintBig  OK (time = 84ms)
     run .../one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf (401ms) Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/FortressLibrary$String
    Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 58.365 sec

`ant testOneLibrary` alone, earlier on the same code: `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 28.692 sec`, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, `Total time: 35 seconds`.

The XXX test, shown red on a deliberate fix: `OneLibraryHalf.fss`'s body changed for one run to `run(): () = ()`, which needs no library class, then restored (`diff` against the saved copy printed nothing):

    cd ProjectFortress && FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one FORTRESS_CACHES=tmp/rung-library-selector/xxx-caches \
        ../bin/fortress junit one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf.test one_library_tests/XXXOneLibraryRunHalf.test
    . run one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf (368ms) Did not see expected failure
    Tests run: 2,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0

As it is, the same pair reports `Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)` in both track runs above.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

The place is the one that `explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md`, B.13, names: the compiled path's library is chosen by `Shell.useCompilerLibraries()` alone, which repoints `WellKnownNames` and `Types`; the run's library is the jars on the class path that `bin/run_classpath` builds. The selector is probe Y's (F-353; `probe-y.md`, section 2), without the parts the batch gives to later rungs (S3, S5, S6) or that probe Y's section 3 marks as hacks of the code generator (7). The other sites of probe Y's two hunks: `useCompilerLibraries()` is the one place every compiled-path command passes (`Shell.java:414-502`); two flags call `WellKnownNames.useCompilerLibraries()` and `Types.useCompilerLibraries()` directly, `-compiler-lib` of `compilerPhases` and of `walk` (`Shell.java:871-874`, `:1118-1121`); they are an explicit choice of the prelude and stay. `Types.useTypeCheckerLibraries()` has no caller. In `build.xml`, `cache0` and `cache1` each stand at seven places (property, two of `cleanCache`, three of `checkCaches`, one of `compileAll`); `cacheOne` stands at the same seven. The caches folder's other readers in `bin/` are `bin/runOpt:32`, the optimizer's runner, which the suites call only with `fortress.unittests.noopt` false (`default_repository/configuration`: true), and `bin/BytecodeOptimizeCompilerTests`, which names the prelude's jars by path; neither follows the selection.

The ways the tree offers, for each choice, are in "Decisions" below.

## What the specification settles

Nothing: the specification names neither a selector nor a caches folder (the grep of the spec line). P-33 and P-37 settle the order and that the prelude stays the default and gains nothing; this rung adds no declaration to any library file.

## Programs run old against new

- The three track tests, under the selection: old above (two refusals), new above (three green).
- Probe Arr (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/programs/Arr.fss`, copied to the scratch), new only, under the selection, for row 1061, whose before is the planner's (PROBES.md, section 6):

      FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one bin/fortress compile Arr.fss
      Exception in thread "main" java.lang.RuntimeException: Not in the trait table: Array1
      Array1 @ .../Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1750:7-11
      rc=1

- Two ladder files whose phase or text moved against the 2026-09-19 baseline, old only, to place the move (below).

## Wrong pairings, and the run under the selection

No mark in a jar stops a wrong pairing (S3). Measured, from `ProjectFortress/`:

    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one bin/fortress compile one_library_tests/OneLibraryHalf.fss    rc=0, 26.5 s; writes default_repository/caches-one/bytecode_cache/OneLibraryHalf.jar
    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one bin/fortress run OneLibraryHalf
      Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/FortressLibrary$String
      Caused by: java.io.IOException: Resource not found : fortress/FortressLibrary$String.class      rc=1
    bin/fortress run OneLibraryHalf                       (no selection: the prelude's caches folder)
      Could not load OneLibraryHalf
      Caused by: java.io.IOException: Resource not found : OneLibraryHalf.class                         rc=1
    FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one bin/fortress run Integer1        (a prelude program, its jar in default_repository/caches)
      Could not load Integer1 ... Resource not found : Integer1.class                                   rc=1
    FORTRESS_CACHES=X bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss; FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one FORTRESS_CACHES=X bin/fortress run Integer1
      PASS                                                                                              rc=0

So a program run against the other library's caches folder is not found ('Could not load P'); with one caches folder named for both, a prelude program runs under the selection as without it, since the run's class path differs only by the caches folder (no second set of classes, S5); and a one-library program dies at its first library class. The property `fortress.library` steers a JVM; the scripts read only the environment variable, so `-Dfortress.library=one` in `JAVA_FLAGS` gives the compile `caches-one` and the run's class path `caches` (the `expand` lines above): a run then finds no jar. Under the selection the compile of a program writes only its own jar; the one library has none (new row NEW-S-1).

# Rung C of climb batch 33: the record lines

## Findings

1. **A primary whose math items all apply in turn to its front compiles: `x[5]^2` is `(x[5])^2`, `g[1][2]` is `(g[1])[2]`, and `Maker.f()[5]^2` and `(mk())[5]^2` likewise.** Conditions: the compiled path, against the compiler's prelude; a subscript before a superscript, or before another subscript, as math items of one primary. Before: the compile stopped, '** bug! Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes.', for each form (the base's `junit.sh fail` run of `SubscriptThenSuperscriptCompiled`; a subscript after a subscript, `g[1][2]` alone, by the probe `SubSubProbe` of REPORT.md). Cause and repair: the checker's reassociation (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala`, `checkExprOperators`, case `SMathPrimary`) returned the one application it left unchecked where no element followed it, and wrote each subscript as a subscript expression, which the code generator refuses (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5729`); it now checks that application at the expected type (`Operators.scala:360-362`) and writes the subscript as a call of the subscript operator's method, as the desugaring before the checker writes every other subscript (`Operators.scala:313-321`; `compiler/desugarer/AssignmentAndSubscriptDesugarer.scala:75-80`). Test: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/SubscriptThenSuperscriptCompiled.test`. Walk still fails on these forms (row 1). What it means: a compiled program may write `x[5]^2` and `x[i][j]`; a program for both paths still writes `(x[5])^2` until row 1 is repaired.
2. **A local tuple binding checks a name's declared type against its element where other names declare none and the right side is no tuple expression.** `(total: ZZ64, part) = two()` for `two(): (ZZ32, ZZ32)` converts the element into `ZZ64` and runs; `(word: String, part) = two()` is refused, 'Right-hand side has type (ZZ32, ZZ32), but declared type is (String, ZZ32).' Before: the first died at run time, `ClassCastException` of an `FZZ32` to `FZZ64`, and the second compiled and printed 8. Repair: the right side is checked again against each name's type (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Decls.scala:431-443`), as the top-level form does (`:324-336`). Tests: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LocalTupleBindingMixedTypes.test` with `LocalTupleBindingMixedTypesLink.test`, and `XXXLocalTupleBindingMixedRefused.test` over `LocalTupleBindingMixedRefused.fss`. Walk gives the same answers: it runs the first and refuses the second when the binding runs, 'RHS expression type ZZ32 is not assignable to LHS type String'. What it means: the local and top-level forms of a tuple binding are typed alike on the compiled path.
3. **A top-level variable declared mutable by `:=` alone satisfies its api's `var` declaration, also as a name of a tuple binding.** `tally: ZZ32 := 0` and `(count, unseen): (ZZ32, ZZ32) := (5, 9)` under `var tally: ZZ32` and `var count: ZZ32`. Before: 'Unmatched declarations: … (var tally:ZZ32, due to different modifiers)'. Repair: the export check compares a top-level variable's modifiers other than `var`, and its mutability as before (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:232-236`), as it compares a field's and a value parameter's (`:697`, `:908`). The team's `compiler_tests/XXX1an.test` still pins 'due to different modifiers, different mutabilities' for `test var y: String` against `y: String = "init"`. Tests: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/TopLevelVarByAssignExport.test`, and `TopLevelVarByAssignImport.test`, which reads and assigns both names through the api and prints PASS, as walk does. What it means: a component may declare an exported mutable variable in either of the specification's spellings (`Specification/basic/variables.tex:85-95`).
4. **A variable bound without a type to a block that ends in a numeral after a local declaration or a local function takes the numeral's default, and a tuple there its elements' defaults.** `x = do k: ZZ32 = 3; 4 end` is a `ZZ32`, `do k: ZZ32 = 3; 0.5 end` an `RR64`, `do g(): ZZ32 = 3; 7 end` a `ZZ32`, and `(a, b) = do k: ZZ32 = 3; (1, k) end` a pair of `ZZ32`. Before: the binding kept `NaturalNumeral[\1,10,4\]`, and a later conversion died, `NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/CompilerBuiltin$v`. Repair: `joinNumerals` and `tupleJoin` read a local declaration's and a local function's body (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:1290-1294`, `:1332-1333`), as `numeralResult` and `joinInto` do. Test: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NumeralEndsUntypedBlockCompiled.test` with `NumeralEndsUntypedBlockCompiledLink.test`; walk prints PASS for its program. # Climb batch 33, rung Q: `self` at a self type or a listed type on the compiled path

- problem: rows 1051, 1050 and 1052 (review-queue item 572), measured on the base through the harness ("The failing and the passing runs" below); `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:1055-1057`; the one library's site `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:291-294`
- spec: `Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:64-80` (the type of `self` is `T ∩ (U1 ∪ … ∪ Un)` under a `comprises` clause, and `T ∩ X` in the bodies of a trait with a self-type parameter `X`); `Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"
- precedent: climb batch 31's rung K, `CodeGen.castToTypeBelow`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:7638` (commit `6df780a7d0`), and its call at a method's returned value, `CodeGen.java:3231`
- deviation: a conditional's arms are cast at the conditional's own static type, which the checker gives the `If` node, not at a declared type (`CodeGen.java:4494`); a local function's result is cast in `localFunctionClosure`, the member that compiles its body for `forLetFn` (`CodeGen.java:4086`), a member the batch record does not name; no new member above `castToTypeBelow`; the class loader reads an owner's class file where the team's code loaded the class (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:268-271`, `:304`)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java`

One launch of this role worked the rung. Commits on `wip/rung-self-arm-closure`: `0e6e0402b9` (the owed expected-failure test), `3f3984e82f` (the fix, the promotions, the self-type closure test), `f2e20db364` (a `case` clause in the arm test; the expected failure of a `typecase` arm), and the commit that adds this report.

## 1. What changed and why

The checker reads `self` in a trait whose `comprises` clause lists types as also a value of the listed type (P-60), and in a trait with a self-type parameter `X` as `T ∩ X` (P-146). Rung K made the code generator cast such a `self` at a call's single argument, a typed binding, an assignment and a method's returned value. Three shapes were left, and each failed when its class loaded:

1. **A conditional's arms (row 1051).** `forIf` emitted each arm and joined them with no cast. One arm left the trait's interface on the stack and the other the listed type's or the parameter's class; the verifier merges them to `Object`, and the `areturn` at the declared type fails: 'VerifyError: Bad return type'. `castToTypeBelow` at the method's return read the conditional's type, which the checker gives as the winning arm's type (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:529-583`), `R` or `T`, not self's, and emitted nothing. Now `forIf` takes the conditional's type (`CodeGen.java:4494`) and calls `castToTypeBelow` on each arm after its code (`:4517` for each `if` and `elif` clause, `:4527` for the `else`). A `case` expression is desugared into a conditional, so its clauses are cast too (a base failure, now passing; section 5).
2. **A closure's result (row 1050).** `forFnExpr` and the closure of a local function returned the body's value with no cast. Now each calls `castToTypeBelow(body, rt)` on the declared return type after the body (`CodeGen.java:3927` in `forFnExpr`, `:4086` in `localFunctionClosure`).
3. **The circular load (row 1052).** An object that lists a trait with a self-type parameter first extends, as its JVM superclass, that trait's default-method class at itself: `public final class …$Pt extends …$\=Shape?…%Pt?$DefaultTraitMethods implements …$\=Shape?…%Pt?` (javap of the test's jar). Defining `Pt` makes the JVM load that superclass, which the loader expands from its template (`InstantiatingClassloader.readAndExpandGenericThing`). In `tagOf(other: S) = other.tag` the template calls `tag` by `invokeinterface` on `S`; with `S` at `Pt`, `MethodInstantiater.visitMethodInsn` called `Class.forName("…$Pt", true, icl)` to learn whether `Pt` is an interface and so choose the opcode, while `Pt` was being defined: 'ClassCircularityError'. Now it reads that answer from the access flags of the class file that the loader would define for the name, through the loader's own resource lookup and ASM's `ClassReader.getAccess()`, and loads no class (`MethodInstantiater.java:268-271`, the new member `interfaceByClassFile` at `:304`). Where no class file is found, as for a class the loader generates, it loads as before. The expanded body then calls `invokevirtual …$Pt.tag`, the opcode that the old code chose wherever its load succeeded.

The cast as built at each place:

| place | where it is emitted | the value cast | the type |
|---|---|---|---|
| a conditional's arm | `CodeGen.java:4517`, `:4527`, after the arm's code and before the jump to the join | the arm's value | the conditional's static type |
| a function expression's result | `CodeGen.java:3927`, before the `areturn` of `apply` | the body's value | the declared return type |
| a local function's result | `CodeGen.java:4086`, before the `areturn` of `apply` | the body's value | the declared return type |

The test that decides whether a cast is emitted is rung K's, unchanged (`CodeGen.java:7638-7660`): the value's static type is the checker's `TraitSelfType` with a non-empty list (or a union each of whose elements is that one type), the target is a trait type or a type variable, the trait opens no sizes, and the target lies strictly below self's trait. So an arm that is not `self`, and an arm whose conditional has self's own type, get none; where the conditional has self's own type, the method's return cast after the join does the work, as before (the `MN` probe, section 5).

The bytecode, from the jars of the tests (javap):

    ComprisesValueAtConditionalArmRun$Q$DefaultTraitMethods.chosen, after:
         4: ifeq          14
         7: aload_0
         8: checkcast     #21                 // class ComprisesValueAtConditionalArmRun$R
        11: goto          25
    SelfTypeArmRun's Tord template, mx?0, after:
        17: aload_0
        18: checkcast     #15                 // class T
        21: goto          25
        24: aload_1
        25: areturn
    SelfTypeFromClosureRun's closure, apply, after:
         1: getfield      #16                 // Field self:LSelfTypeFromClosureRun$Shape?S?;
         4: checkcast     #20                 // class S
         7: areturn

A conditional that needs no cast compiles to the same bytecode as before. A program with `both(c): R = if c then self else self end` and `other(c, r: R): R = if c then r else R(0, 0) end` in `trait Q comprises { R }`, and a top-level `pick(c, a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if c then a else b end`, compiled on the base and on the edit: `diff` of the `javap -c -p` of `NoCastIf$Q$DefaultTraitMethods` and of `NoCastIf` prints nothing. `both` reads, before and after:

         4: ifeq          11
         7: aload_0
         8: goto          12
        11: aload_0
        12: checkcast     #21                 // class NoCastIf$R
        15: areturn

(the one `checkcast` is the return cast after the join, rung K's), and `pick` has no `checkcast`.

## 2. The failing and the passing runs

The owed test first, `compiler_tests/XXXSelfTypeArmRun.test` with `SelfTypeArmRunLink.test` (`0e6e0402b9`), on the base's code, 2026-11-17T18:36:20Z:

## What changed and why

Three edits of `CodeGen.java`, at commit `18d5b51578` (tests first in `33f3e89713`):

1. **The constructor** (`CodeGen.java:498-502`). For each type of the component, the code generator reads the methods that the type inherits, to find the functional methods it must emit for it (`STypesUtil.properlyInheritedMethodsNotIdenticallyCovered`). It read them with the component's analyzer, whose kind environment holds no static parameter. Where a supertype's `comprises` clause lists a type at a `where`-clause variable, the subtype test that compares two inherited methods' owners opens that variable and compares it with the type's own parameter (`TypeAnalyzer.pSubInner`, `scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:208` and `:225`, through `:281` and `:298`), and the lookup of that parameter stops: `TypeAnalyzer.scala:1102`. The edit reads them with the type's static parameters and `where` clause in the kind environment. This is row 812's site (`P812b`, below: 'Y is not in the kind env', `Y` the object `Ci`'s own parameter).
2. **A generic function's or generic method's body** (`GenericMethodBodyMakerFnDecl.generateGenericMethodBody`, `CodeGen.java:2749-2756`). The template's body was compiled by a `CodeGen` whose analyzer held only the enclosing trait's or object's parameters, never the function's own. The edit compiles it in a nested `CodeGen` whose analyzer holds the declaration's static parameters and `where` clause; for a generic method the declaration is `convertGenericMethodToClosureDecl`'s, whose parameters are the receiver's parameter, the method's own and the trait's (`CodeGen.java:2890-2893`). Behind the constructor's wall stood this one: a dotted call, in a generic body, of a member of a type below a `where`-clause `comprises`, at a type that names the function's parameter, stops in `methodsNamed` (`CodeGen.java:7069`), from `callTakesTupleBoxed` (`P812g`, below), the path that F-34 names behind `ArrayList` (`genericMethodTakesOneParameter` reaches `methodsNamed` too).
3. **`forTypecase`** (`CodeGen.java:2541-2546`, new members `namesTupleElements` and `bindElementsAndGenerateClauseBody` at `:2578-2610`). The code generator bound a clause's own name (`x: T =>`, row 351's repair) but left unbound the names of a clause's tuple pattern, `(a': T, b': U) =>`. A read of such a name fell to `forVarRef`'s fresh-import path, which treats the name as a top-level variable and normalizes its type (`CodeGen.java:6933`): in a generic function, where the type names the function's parameters, that normalization stopped, 'T is not in the kind env' — row 822's recorded stack, `CodeGen.forVarRef`, `TypeAnalyzer.normalize`. Outside a generic function the read compiles, as a field of a class `P$s` that does not exist, and the run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError` (new row NEW-V-1). The edit casts the matched tuple to the clause's tuple type, as the clause's own name is cast (`InstantiatingClassloader.generalizedCastTo`), and binds each name of the pattern, `_` excepted, to its element, by the tuple's element getter, as a local binding of a tuple to several names does (`CodeGen.java:4765`).

The scope the repair gives: a type's inherited methods, and a generic function's or method's body, are read with the static parameters and `where`-clause variables in scope there; a typecase clause's tuple-pattern names are bound on the compiled path, in any function. Not covered: the body of a function without static parameters whose `where` clause introduces a variable (no test needs it; row 867 holds such a call), and the wrappers that `forObjectDecl` emits for an object's functional methods (`CodeGen.java:4797-4820`), which read the component's analyzer.

- problem: ledger row 540, a method call on a call typed by the intersection of its candidates' return types crashes `fortress compile` with `ClassCastException`, `IntersectionType` to `NamedType` (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:177`); the one library's `__filter` is the code generator's one refused declaration of this kind on the base's code (F-34, `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:38`; `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/switch-rehearsal.md:189`).
- spec: `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:627-628`, the intersection of a set of types is a subtype of every type of the set, so a value of the intersection has each conjunct's methods; with `Specification/basic/expressions/method-invocation.tex:47-48`, the receiver is bound to the method's `self`.
- precedent: `castToTypeBelow` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:7630` on the base), which casts a value whose checker type the JVM does not know through `InstantiatingClassloader.generalizedCastTo` (`:7652`); `emitBodyGivenBy`'s most specific trait by `typeAnalyzer.lteq` over `methodsNamed` (`:7088-7091`); the name test of `Types.sameName` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Types.java:112`).
- deviation: the owner is narrowed to the conjuncts that have the declaration the checker chose, read from the arrow's `MethodInfo` (`CodeGen.java:7476-7491`), which the fork's wording does not name; among owners none of which lies below the others the first in the intersection's order is taken (`:7500`); the generic-method branch gets the owner too (`:7297`); the helpers stand as new members directly below `sanitizePossibleStupidIntersectionType` (`:7461-7523`); an intersection with no owner among its conjuncts stops with 'Can't find the owner of m among the conjuncts of T' (`:7493`) where the base threw `ClassCastException`. The specification's spelling: none.
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`.

One launch worked this rung: the worktree did not exist at the start.

## 1. What changed and why

`CodeGen.forMethodInvocation` took the receiver's static type, narrowed an intersection to its lowest conjunct where the conjuncts nest (`sanitizePossibleStupidIntersectionType`, `CodeGen.java:7420` on the base), and otherwise kept the intersection and cast it to `NamedType` (`:7323`) or, for a generic method, to `TraitType` (`:7270`, and again in `emitFindGenericMethodClosure`, `:7497`). The checker types a call whose argument stands between two closed traits by the intersection of its candidates' return types (P-60), and a `typecase` binder whose arm's type neither lies below nor above the selector's type by the intersection of the two, so every method call on such a value crashed the compile.

The edit, all in `CodeGen.java` (`git diff 1609258002b0 -- ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, 73 lines added, none removed):

- `forMethodInvocation` (`:7215-7221`): where the sanitized receiver type is still an `IntersectionType`, it is replaced by its owner, `intersectionMethodOwner`, and that trait is kept as `receiverCast`.
- After the receiver is evaluated, in the generic branch (`:7297`) and the plain branch (`:7323`), `castReceiver(receiverCast)` casts it to the owner. Everything after reads the owner as the receiver's type: the opcode and the class of `methodCall`, the closure's receiver type of a generic method, the tuple boxing test.
- `intersectionMethodOwner` (`:7461-7501`): the trait-type conjuncts, nested intersections opened (`traitConjuncts`, `:7503-7510`), the same conjuncts the checker searches (`traitTypesCallable`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Common.scala:90-104`). A conjunct qualifies if it declares or inherits a method of the call's name (`methodsNamed`), and, where the call's arrow carries a `MethodInfo`, one whose declaring trait is the trait that the arrow names (`sameTraitName`, `:7512-7517`). Of the qualifying conjuncts, the one below all the others; else the first.
- `castReceiver` (`:7519-7523`): `generalizedCastTo` to the class that `methodCall` names (`NamingCzar.jvmTypeDesc(owner, thisApi(), false)`, as at `:629`), a `CHECKCAST` for a trait or object.

The checker is not touched: its typing stays (P-60, fork I1).

Commits on `wip/rung-intersection-receiver`: `2e1dcbaa2d` (the test promoted and the fix), `e0a5274db2` (the typecase-binder test), `875e23e726` (three whitespace-only lines of `CodeGen.java` put back as the base had them; the Edit tool had emptied them; `javac -g` of the file before and after gives the same 15 class files, byte for byte, compared with `cmp`).

## 3. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

# Climb batch 33, rung D: the record lines

The lines the gather folds into the record, from `REPORT.md` beside this file. Row numbers NEW-D-1 and NEW-D-2 are placeholders that the gather numbers.

## Findings

1. **A `typecase` arm whose name binds no type variable in scope and no declared type is refused when names are bound, on both paths: 'X is undefined.', at the name.** Holds for the bare arm `Id =>` and for a name inside an arm's type that no binding rewrite takes (in an arrow type, as `NoSuchArgType -> ZZ32 =>`, or a static argument, as `Maybe[\NoSuchStaticArg\] =>`). Evidence: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/disambiguator/TypeDisambiguator.java:398-406` (`handleTypeName`) and `:241-249` (`forTypecaseClause`); tests `ProjectFortress/tests/TypecaseUndefinedArmWalk.fss` (row 959's walk test promoted) and `compiler_tests/XXXTypecaseUndefinedArmCompiled.test`, `tests/TypecaseUndefinedNameInArmTypeWalk.fss` and `compiler_tests/XXXTypecaseUndefinedNameInArmTypeCompiled.test`. On 1609258002's code the bare arm took every value on both paths (probe `typecase v of Int => ...` for `v: Any = 2.5` printed 'an Int' under walk and compiled), walk loaded an arm with an undefined name in an arrow type or a static argument and failed only when the arm ran ('Missing type NoSuchArg'), the checker refused the arrow form 'Unbound type: NoSuchArgType' and compiled the static-argument form with no message. What it means: an old program's arm at `Int`, `Long`, `Float`, `BigNum` or `UnsignedLong` is refused instead of answering wrongly; a binder over every value is written with its type, `x: Any =>`.
2. **An arm at a type parameter in scope still tests the value against the parameter's static argument.** `handleTypeName` takes a name that `_env.hasTypeParam` finds as a type variable before it looks for a declaration (`TypeDisambiguator.java:392-393`). Tests `tests/TypecaseTypeParamArmWalk.fss` and `compiler_tests/TypecaseTypeParamArmCompiled.test` pass on 1609258002's code and after; the library's `instanceOf[\T\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:39-43`) has this arm.
3. **The tuple of names keeps the team's binding form: an element of a tuple arm whose name no declaration defines binds, so it takes a value of every type** (row NEW-D-1). Under walk `(NoSuchTypeHere, ZZ32) =>` takes `("s", 3)` and `(2.5, 3)` (`tests/TypecaseTupleArmUndefinedNameBindsWalk.fss`, which passes on 1609258002's code and after). `TypeDisambiguator.java:246-256` spares exactly the elements of a tuple arm, at any depth of nested tuples, which `typeToPatternBinding` rewrites into binders. The chapter's grammar reads `(TypeList)` as types (`Specification/basic/expressions/typecase.tex:69-71`) and its note defers patterns to the pattern-matching proposal (`:15`); no decision covers the form. A question for the curator.
4. **Under walk a tuple arm of a name and a type binds the name to the whole selector** (row NEW-D-2): `(first, ZZ32) => first` gives `("s", 3)` for `("s", 3)`, while `(first, second)` binds each element (`tests/TypecaseTupleArmMixedBinderWalk.fss`, today's answer). Compiled, the name is unbound, as row 498 has it: `NoClassDefFoundError: PArmTupleMixedC$first` on 1609258002's code.
5. **Under walk a tuple pattern with an untyped binder, `typecase p of (x, y: ZZ32) =>`, stops when it runs: 'typecase match failure!'; `(x: ZZ32, y: ZZ32)` runs** (probes on 1609258002's code and after: 'typecase match failure!' and 'typed pattern 3 4'). Row 964 holds the code generator's stop on the same clause; the note below adds walk.
6. **Walk's harness counts a static error of the phases as a refusal at load.** A walk test's `.test` with `load_` keys is green when the phases refuse the program with a static error that meets the keys, as when walk's load check refuses it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:870-878`, `InterpreterTest.thrownAtLoad`). Before, only an exception under `Driver.evalComponent` counted, so no `.test` could name a refusal of the disambiguator or another phase. Test: `tests/TypecaseUndefinedArmWalk.test`, which on 1609258002's harness read 'Failed after load' for the refusal. No existing walk test's verdict changes: a green plain test's refusal was already under `evalComponent`, and an `XXX` test's verdict reads only whether the program ran clean.
7. **The checker count and the distance do not move.** On 74ebf6a8c0's code the count table equals `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-31b/gate/checker-count.txt` (`#total 0`, `#crash none`), and `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh` prints 'DISTANCE SAME   0' against `climb-batch-31b/gate/distance.txt`; no site moved. No arm of either library names an undefined type: the instrumented scan of REPORT.md, section 6, found none in `Library/`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/` or the compiler's prelude.

## For FACTS

- **A `typecase` arm whose name names no type is refused when names are bound, on both paths: 'X is undefined.'; an arm at a type parameter in scope tests against its static argument, and only an element of a tuple of names still binds.** The disambiguator, which both paths run, resolves a clause's type as every other type: the bare arm `Id =>`, and a name in an arrow type or static argument inside the arm, that binds no type variable in scope and no declared type is a static error at the name (`compiler/disambiguator/TypeDisambiguator.java`, `forTypecaseClause` and `handleTypeName`).
